newsitem.title: CANADA: UGG says asks regulators to probe bid.
newsitem.headline: UGG says asks regulators to probe bid.

text.p: United Grain Growers Ltd president Ted Allen said on Tuesday the company asked securities commissions in three Canadian provinces to review the legality of a C$172 million hostile takeover bid for UGG by Alberta Wheat Pool and Manitoba Pool Elevators.
"We've asked the Ontario, Manitoba and Alberta Securities Commissions to investigate the Pools' bid," Allen told reporters in a conference call.
UGG directors on February 14 adopted a share dilution plan in case any shareholder acquired more than 15 percent of its stock.

The Pools' lock-up deal promptad UGG to say that the "poison pill" was triggered and would take effect on March 4. At that time, each UGG share except those held by the Pools, would carry the right to buy up to 8.5 more shares at C$5.88 each. The Pools have said the poison pill was not triggered.
"An application was filed with Manitoba's Court of Queen's Bench (Tuesday) afternoon and we're waiting for their response on hearing dates (on the poison pill issue)," Martin added.
Allen compared the indebted Pools' bid for UGG to "two drowning men trying to save the lifeguard."
The Pools' C$13.75 a share bid "doesn't reflect the capital investment we've made," he added.
UGG stock ended up 0.15 at 14.30 on the Toronto Stock Exchange on Tuesday.
